en.title: CSSBuy Parcel Evidence Pack 2026: Build a Proof Trail Before International Shipping
en.excerpt: Create a compact evidence file covering the W2C link, warehouse QC, parcel measurements, route selection, tracking and delivery condition before a problem appears.
body: Why a parcel problem is usually an evidence problem

A CSSBuy parcel can move through several independent systems: the seller, the warehouse, the packing team, the international line, customs and the last-mile carrier. When something goes wrong, each system sees only part of the story. That is why the most useful preparation is not another vague promise from a seller or a screenshot of one tracking page. It is a compact evidence file that shows what you ordered, what reached the warehouse, what was packed, which route you paid for and what happened after dispatch. This approach matters because CSSBuy separates order enquiries from parcel enquiries. Purchase verification, returns and refunds belong with the relevant order, while tracking problems and parcel details belong with the relevant parcel. A clean evidence file lets you use the right channel without rewriting the entire history every time. It also protects you from a common memory problem: two weeks after parcel submission, it becomes surprisingly hard to remember which packaging was removed, which item was exchanged and which weight was only an estimate.
Start the file before the listing changes

Open the evidence file when you decide to buy, not after a dispute begins. Save the original W2C link, seller name, product title, selected color, size, model, quantity and the price shown when you submitted the order. Record Chinese domestic shipping separately from the product price. If the listing uses confusing option names, add a short plain-English description such as navy, size XL, embroidered back, no gift box. This is especially useful on marketplace listings that can be edited, removed or reused. A future screenshot may not show the same option set you saw when ordering. Your order snapshot should therefore include the date, the exact selected variant and any seller promise that changed the decision. Do not save hundreds of images. One product-page screenshot, one variant screenshot and one note explaining the non-negotiable details are normally enough. The purpose is not to create a legal archive. It is to make the order verifiable when the warehouse item arrives.
Separate seller evidence from warehouse evidence

Seller photos describe what is being offered; warehouse QC photos show the physical item that arrived. Keep those two evidence groups separate. Marketing images may be useful for checking the intended model, color placement and included accessories, but they do not prove the condition of your own item. Warehouse images are stronger for order matching, visible defects and measurements, yet they still cannot prove long-term durability or every hidden material. Create a simple status line for each item: ordered, arrived, QC reviewed, extra photo requested, approved, exchange requested, return requested or removed from haul. That one line prevents accidental approval and makes mixed-seller hauls much easier to manage. When multiple products arrive on different days, the status line also shows which item is delaying parcel submission and whether waiting is still worth the storage time.
Turn QC photos into a decision record

Do not merely download QC images. Write the decision they support. For clothing, record the measured chest, length, sleeve or waist when fit matters. For shoes, note size tags, visible symmetry and any requested insole measurement. For bags or accessories, record dimensions, hardware condition and missing parts. If a photograph does not answer the approval question, request a targeted image instead of asking for more QC. A useful QC note follows one sentence: approve if X is confirmed; exchange or return if Y is visible. For example, approve if the chest measures at least 60 cm and the rear embroidery is centered; return if the print is cracked. This keeps the inspection standard stable. Without a prewritten standard, buyers often lower expectations simply because the item has already reached the warehouse. The evidence file should make the decision easier, not justify every purchase.
Record the shipping assumptions before paying the deposit

CSSBuy explains that the international shipping deposit is based on estimated weight, the chosen method and the destination, while the final amount is calculated from the package size and weight verified later. Record both the estimate and the final parcel profile. Your file should include actual weight, length, width, height, calculated volumetric weight, chargeable weight, route name and destination. The current CSSBuy estimator also notes that many freight lines charge the larger of actual and volumetric weight, with divisors such as 5,000 or 6,000 depending on the route. Treat the divisor as route-specific data, not a universal formula. If your parcel contains bulky boxes, structured bags or light but oversized products, add a volume-risk note before submission. This helps explain later why a parcel with modest scale weight received a higher chargeable weight.
Freeze the parcel manifest

Before paying international shipping, create a final parcel manifest. List every included order number, item name, quantity and packaging choice. Mark anything removed from the parcel, returned to the seller or intentionally left in storage. If you asked for vacuum packaging, reinforcement, box removal or special protection, record that instruction beside the affected item. This step catches several expensive errors: an item approved in QC but omitted from the parcel, a returned item accidentally included, two similar orders confused with each other, or a fragile product packed without the requested reinforcement. The manifest also gives you a fast way to check the delivered box. You should be able to compare the received contents with one page instead of opening months of order history.
Save route, restriction and declaration details

Record the shipping line exactly as displayed, the estimated delivery range, tracking method, route restrictions and the declaration information you submitted. Keep this compliance-focused. A declaration is not a trick for avoiding destination rules; it should reasonably describe the parcel and follow the requirements shown for the route and country. CSSBuy's estimator warns that designer-branded goods, liquids, powders and batteries can be restricted on selected methods, so note any sensitive attribute that affected route eligibility. If your preferred method does not appear, or the declaration screen is unclear, resolve that before payment. Do not rely on an old recommendation from another country or a parcel with different contents. The evidence file should capture the route that was actually available for your parcel on the date you submitted it. Shipping options and rules can change, and a screenshot of the final selection is more useful than a general forum comment.
Document packaging trade-offs

Packaging decisions should show both the requested saving and the accepted risk. Vacuum packaging may reduce volume for soft clothing, while reinforced packaging can improve protection for fragile products. Removing boxes may reduce weight or dimensions, but it can also reduce structure and presentation. Write down why you made the choice. A practical note might read: remove outer shoe boxes, keep internal stuffing, reinforce corners; or vacuum-pack clothing only, do not compress the structured jacket. Clear notes reduce ambiguity and make it easier to assess a damage claim later. If the delivered item is crushed, your own record will show whether protective packaging was requested, removed or never available. The goal is not to assign blame automatically; it is to preserve the facts.
Build a tracking timeline after dispatch

Once the parcel ships, switch from the order file to a tracking timeline. Record the dispatch date, first tracking event, export event, customs event, destination handoff and delivery attempt. Do not panic over every quiet period, but note changes that are materially different from the route's displayed estimate. CSSBuy states that delays, taxes, confiscation, damage and missing parcels can occur while third-party logistics companies or customs control the shipment. That means a useful timeline should distinguish no new scan from a confirmed exception. Save screenshots when the carrier displays a return, damage, customs request or delivery confirmation that conflicts with what happened. A timeline with dates is much more actionable than a message saying the parcel has been stuck for a long time.
When the parcel arrives damaged or incomplete

Photograph the unopened exterior before cutting tape if there is visible crushing, water damage, puncture or resealing. Then photograph the shipping label, every side of the carton, the internal packing and the affected products. Keep the original packaging until the issue is documented. For missing items, compare the delivered contents with the frozen manifest and warehouse records before assuming theft or packing error. Write a concise incident summary: parcel number, delivery date, visible condition, missing or damaged item, evidence available and the outcome requested. Avoid sending twenty unlabelled photos. Name or number the images so support can follow the sequence. If the issue concerns tracking, logistics or parcel details, use the relevant parcel and Add Note. If it concerns a purchase, warehouse verification, return or refund, use the relevant order and Add Note. The right channel saves time.
A claim-ready evidence pack in twelve lines

Your final evidence pack can remain compact. Include: 1) W2C link and seller; 2) ordered variant; 3) price and domestic freight; 4) seller instructions; 5) warehouse arrival date; 6) QC decision and measurements; 7) approved parcel manifest; 8) package weight and dimensions; 9) route and declaration snapshot; 10) packaging instructions; 11) tracking timeline; and 12) delivery-condition photos if needed. Store the file in a folder named with the parcel number. That simple naming rule becomes valuable when you have several shipments. The best evidence system is not the most complicated one. It is the one you can complete before payment and understand quickly when a problem appears.
FAQ: Do I need to save every QC photo?

No. Keep the standard set, plus any extra image that directly supports a sizing, defect, accessory or packaging decision. A short note explaining what the images prove is more useful than a large unorganized folder.
FAQ: Is the shipping deposit the final price?

Not necessarily. CSSBuy states that the deposit uses estimated weight, the selected method and destination, while the final shipping fee uses package size and weight verified by the shipping company. Record both figures and any later account adjustment.
FAQ: Should I contact support through My Order or My Parcel?

Use My Order and Add Note for purchasing, shipment verification, returns and refunds. Use My Parcel and Add Note for tracking, logistics updates and parcel details. Include the relevant order or parcel number in the evidence summary.
FAQ: Can packaging removal change a restricted item into an ordinary item?

No. Removing a box can change weight or volume, but it does not change whether the product contains a battery, liquid, powder, magnet or another restricted attribute. Route eligibility should be checked using the product itself.
FAQ: What should I photograph after delivery?

If there is a problem, photograph the unopened outer carton, shipping label, damaged areas, internal packing and affected items. For missing contents, also photograph everything received and compare it with the parcel manifest.
FAQ: How long should I keep the file?

Keep it until the parcel has been delivered, inspected and any after-sales issue is closed. For high-value or complicated hauls, retaining the manifest and final cost record longer can help with future planning.
